pages.transcription:
New Haven, Hotel Taft
Dear Hannah and Manfred, Lotte phoned yesterday with your daughter
and we heard with pleasure that she feels happy and also the new school
- the public school in which she is now going as the progressive school was
no more scholarship available - seems to please her. She is there the youn-
gest of all, the nearest to her a boy which will be 13 soon. Perhaps she
will have to work harder there as in New-Rochelle, but she will manage it,
I am quite sure. Mr. Salmon has invited her for the week end and I hope
she will enjoy it very much, meeting her schoolfellows. She will have
her school holidays in March and we will do our possible to see her then
or to have her with us.
We are living here in a little, not very artistic town, but I have all
facilities at the Yale University. I can take as many books at home
as I like and you may imagine, how helpful this is; the head librarian is
a charming man and we have been invited in his house; today Thornton
Wilder is coming, yesterday and last week Shalom Asch and Joachim
Maas - you see, we live not in a wilderness, but I have time to read and
to write.
As you are managing all my things I would ask you to send
through my bank eighteen Pounds to Max H. Bresch consultant
on International Law Ibex-House, Minories London EC 3 which
amount I am due for a consultation of his American office. Con-
cerning all other things I shall write directly to my chartered
accountant Mr. Wilmot. As to the house I know that all is there
in best order; please give my best regards to Mr. Miller and all
the good helpers. Sometimes we are weary of this Hotel life but
there are such difficulties with apartments - service etc - that we
must continue. Perhaps in Rio, where everything is cheaper and easier
than here. But who can make plans? We live and wait and wait
and live, so dont let us wait to long for good news that you have
a well merited rest at Bath. Love to all. Yours Stefan Zweig
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf rosa Papier. Sehr gut lesbar.
